title: Having way too much fun!
author: inigid
selftext:
I think I saw someone was saying the other day, having AI as a thought partner and collaborator is bringing out their inner child again.

I couldn't agree more!

I'm having a blast building all kinds of fun stuff.

I just added a new WASM based plugin system to my raytracer engine, Matryoshka yesterday, so now you can write Actors in whatever language you like and attach them to world items.

The plugins can control the entities, and they can also create geometry, textures, or even take part in particle simulation as well.

This morning I was messing about and made this little test scene.

I have one plugin generating the level as the player moves around, another controlling the NPCs, another one for the vehicles, a separate one for the high level traffic system, and finally one for the overhead drone.

Once you build one then they can be infinitely reused, so you get a kind of flywheel effect over time.

Anyway, it's just a test, and as you can see I didn't make the collision volume on the NPCs wide enough, but it is okay for now I think.

I used Kenney libraries for the tiles, and these are what get placed by the procedural generation system.

That uses a stable spatial hash, so you can wander off and come back and it will look the same.

I also roll off simulation of the characters based on distance so the world doesn't have to tick every NPC at the same rate.  Only ones directly in view receive per frame updates, with a distance falloff.

Hope everyone is having fun building.  Have a great weekend!

Enjoy having a wander around Toy Town with me!

comments.author: Pimpwtp
comments.body: Yes imagine what your inner child could do when it learns to build it all themselves

replies.author: JrButton
replies.body: Let us know how that goes for you. We'll eagerly wait to see what you accomplish

replies.author: Pimpwtp
replies.body: Thats alright I already spend 2 years on a project, then gave up, and working on a new one again. Even if it never sees the day of light, the experience and process are worth so much. A.I. enthusiasts will never understand.

replies.author: DoggoDadagon
replies.body: I have 6 years into my game, fuck that, I want it finished and out there.

replies.author: JrButton
replies.body:
See, that's where you're probably wrong. You're ignoring (conveniently I might add) the past of those you're so eager to judge/criticize.

I for example spent 2 years also working on a game/project of my own. Picked up a new one that's actually doing incredibly well right now and due to the benefits of AI I was able to stand up my old project in a matter of hours and bring it mostly across the finish line.

I spent countless hours learning blender back in the day, and built several models for our game while my bro in law built most of the mechanics using unreal... we both spent time learning the craft to do it all, but felt it best we specialized for faster delivery. Well, eventually I had to get into texturing our models and that's where things came to a grinding halt.

This was several years ago (\~10-15) and the assets/resources available to even unreal and the time weren't what they are today... needless to say we retired our efforts.

Do I understand the value of experiencing the process you're referring to? Uh, yea. What I'm not is an idiot swearing off AI and the value it brings to helping people do wild and cool stuff. Stop being a troglodyte or if you want to keep with that anti AI narrative, at least stop judging others for learning it.

AI simply enables smart people to do incredible things. Not any average joe can accomplish most of what you're seeing in these threads... AI is only as smart as the person using it.

Right now you're no different than the guys standing in the streets of New York in the early 1900's claiming anyone using automobiles were bad, stupid, or dumb... guess who really ended up being bad, stupid, and dumb

replies.author: inigid
replies.body: Well I have spent decades professionally doing that.  Is it okay if it for once don't have to do it all alone tapping away on the details when I have bigger stuff in my head.  Is that okay with you?  I'm sure you want me to spend the last few years of my life having access to modern technology and tools.  I'm getting on a bit you know.

replies.author: Pimpwtp
replies.body: And that didn't "bring out your inner child"? What's the difference then for you?

replies.author: inigid
replies.body:
The difference is I have a lot more to get written down before I die, and typing it all out just isn't cutting it.  I'm still up until 4am.  But now I can get a 100x more done in the same amount of time.

It's not even apples to apples because I simply wouldn't have the energy to even attempt this otherwise because of the enormity of it.  So it's essentially infinite to 1 amplification compared to not doing it at all.

Have you ever had a situation like that, where you thought, gosh, I would love to do xyz, but the energy and resources required simply make the attempt impossible.  I'll be here years and still no guarantee if it works.

For me and a lot of other people, AI provides the helping hand and assist to put childhood dreams within reach.

It isn't as if I didn't know how to do it.  Clearly I did otherwise I wouldn't even know how to approach the entire project.   It's simply the sheer scale of doing it makes it impossible within any reasonable time.

It isn't clear to me why you are irked that I'm happy with what I made in collaboration with modern tooling.

I mean, would it make you happier to think of me not being able to build stuff, and just sit here struggling for the sake of it, decaying until I give in.

That's not my idea of fun, and it isn't something I would wish on anyone.

People should have whatever assistance they need in no matter what form.

If you are against that, I'm not really sure what to tell you.

I have nothing against struggling, but some stuff is struggling more as a penance and virtue signaling.

I don't wash my clothes in the river either anymore.  But I suppose I could if it makes you happy.

replies.author: Pimpwtp
replies.body: I understand what you say and I appreciate you actually writing it down. I guess I just can't fathom the concept of all these thoughts actually being "worthy" of your time if that makes sense. Either something is good and it deserves the effort or it was just a little brainfart in the first place. But it's ok we don't have to value the same things.  Thank you for answering and good luck on the project.

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.
